title: Console onboarding tour: first-run checklist, empty-state visuals, and contextual tips
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Design a lightweight, developer-focused first-run experience in the Console that reduces initial confusion, surfaces key features (API keys, model catalog, dedicated capacity), and provides defensible empty states for teams with no projects. Deliverables: 1) First-run checklist modal + progressive checklist states (dismissible, persistent) 2) Empty states for Projects, API Keys, Destinations, and Model Routes with clear CTAs 3) Contextual inline tips (tooltip/pill) for advanced settings like Dedicated and Private deployment 4) Graphic assets and a small screenshot pack for release notes and marketing 5) Localization-ready microcopy and accessibility annotations.
design_notes:
- Emphasize progressive disclosure: keep checklist 3–4 steps max. Primary CTA binds to 'Create project' or 'Get API key'.
- Use single-column modal with left-side progress column (step title + short blurb).
- Empty states should include small code snippet for 'quickstart snippet' to reduce time-to-first-success.
- Visual language consistent with console brand tokens: neutral gray background, 48px hero icon, 16px supporting text.
- Provide 2 art directions for hero illustration: 'developer-first' (monochrome device + terminal) and 'platform overview' (stacked layers with callouts).
- Accessibility: ensure color contrast AA, focusable dismiss link, and ARIA labels for checklist steps.
- Performance: keep assets under 400KB per image; provide SVG + PNG fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Checklist modal present on first sign-in for new orgs and can be re-opened from 'Help > Getting started'.
2) Each checklist step is actionable and verified by the product events team (analytics events recorded on click).
3) Empty states show suggested next steps, include a one-line code snippet, and link to docs.
4) All microcopy approved by content and localized for en, fr, de (placeholders acceptable for initial rollout).
5) Figma files with component variants, tokenized styles, and exportable assets provided to frontend.
6) Accessibility audit sign-off (contrast, keyboard, screen reader labels).
